title: Analysis of the Derivatives of Sialic Acid in Pig Tissues
author: Chon-Ho Yen

steps_raw.instruction: SOP : Analysis of the Derivatives of Sialic Acid in Pig Tissues

Introdction：Sialic acid is a generic term for the N- or O-substituted derivatives of neuraminic acid, a monosaccharide with a nine-carbon backbone. N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc or NGNA) is not synthesized in the human body, so most of the sialic acid in the body is N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac or NANA), while other animals have two kinds of sialic acid (NANA and NGNA). There may be NGNA in biotech products manufactured from nonhuman animal source, and a detectable method is needed to determine the derivatives of sialic acid in the product.
Purpose： The detection method of sialic acid by HPLC Analysis, and further distinguish the NGNA and NANA of sialic acid in biotechnology products.
Material/reagent and device：
HPLC system, Thermo Scientific™ (Waters 2475 Multi-wavelength Fluorescence Detector, Waters 717 plus Autosampler and Waters 600 Controller)
Reversed phase C18 column (DiscoveryR BIO wide Pore C18, 5m, 4.6 x 25 cm)
Dry Bath Incubator (Violet BioScience Inc. Model VH01)
Centrifuge (Sigma 3K30)
0.22m membrane (Millipore GVWP04700)
DMB (1, 2-diamino 4, 5-methylenedioxybenzene) reagent

Prepare reagent buffer : Add 99.8% of Acetic acid 800L , 540L 2-ME and 31 mg Sodium hydrosulfite dissolved in 7 mL deionized water and add water to the final volume of 10 mL. (1.4 M acetic acid, 0.75M 2-mercaptoethanol and 18 mM Sodium hydrosulfite solution)
Add 1.6 mg DMB ( purchase from Sigma-Aldrich, Inc.) into 1 mL of reagent buffer.
HPLC elution Buffer (MeOH / Acetonitrile /H2O=7:9:84) :
Added 100% methanol 70 mL and 90 mL of Acetonitrile into 1 L volumetric flask then add deionized water to final volume of 1000 mL. The solution is filtered through 0.22m membrane.
About 100 mg samples, including ear or tail tissues and small intestines, in MQ water are cut into small pieces by scissors.
The mixture is incubated at 95 oC for 30 min.
After cooling to room temperature, 0.5 M H2SO4 was added to the final concentration of 25 mM.
The mixtures were incubated at 80 oC for 1 h to release the sialic acids from the samples.
After centrifugation at 10,000 x g for 10 min, the supernatant was collected.
Prepare the standard: 1 mg of NANA and NGNA is dissolve in 1 mL of deionized water, respectively.
200 L of DMB reagent are added to	200 L of samples and standard, respectively, the mixture are incubated at 80 oC for 2 h to label fluorescent agent.
After labelling, the mixtures are filtrated through 0.22m membrane.

The DMB-labeled sample was injected onto Waters™ HPLC system (Waters 2475 Multi-wavelength Fluorescence Detector, Waters 717 plus Autosampler and Waters 600 Controller) with the DiscoveryⓇ BIO wide Pore C18 (5 m, 4.6 x 25 cm) column.

The analysis was performed by an isocratic mobile phase of Methanol: Acetonitrile: H2O ratio are 7: 9: 84 with a flow rate of 0.6 mL/min and the fluorescence detector was set at excitation wavelength of 373 nm and emission wavelength of 448 nm.
Usually, the samples are diluted 100 folds and the standards are diluted 5000-10000 folds with deionized water for HPLC analysis.
